Alchemy.what: Vials and herbs for the first potions and elixirs (Earthroot for Lion's Strength).
Alchemy.why: Alchemists brew healing and mana potions, elixirs that strengthen body and mind, and later transmute one material into another. Their potions are among the most valued supplies an adventurer can carry.

Blacksmithing.what: The hammer the first recipes need, copper bars, and stone for sharpening stones.
Blacksmithing.why: Blacksmiths forge weapons and mail and plate armour from metal bars, and make the sharpening and weight stones every fighter uses. A smith keeps their own gear in shape and is always in demand among soldiers.

Cooking.what: Raw meat for the first recipes (Charred Wolf Meat, Spiced Wolf Meat, Roasted Boar Meat). In 3.3.5 the Basic Campfire needs no Flint and Tinder or wood, and these recipes need no spices.
Cooking.why: A good cook turns plain meat and fish into hearty meals that leave a traveller well fed and stronger for hours on the road. Cooks are welcome at every campfire, and their dishes always find a buyer.

Enchanting.what: Everything for the Runed Copper Rod (Copper Rod, Strange Dust, Lesser Magic Essence), which every enchantment needs, plus dust for the first enchantments.
Enchanting.why: Enchanters break unwanted magic items down into dust and essences and use them to imbue weapons and armour with lasting power. Every adventurer wants their gear enchanted, so a good enchanter never lacks work.

Engineering.what: The hammer the first recipes need (bolts, tubes, and the Arclight Spanner itself), copper bars, and stone for blasting powder.
Engineering.why: Engineers build gadgets, explosives, guns and scopes, and later even mechanical mounts and devices that can carry them across the world. Their inventions are unpredictable, sometimes dangerous, and never dull.

First Aid.why: Anyone who can bind a wound with clean linen keeps themselves and their companions alive when no healer is near. It costs little to learn, and the cloth for bandages comes from the enemies a traveller fights anyway.

Fishing.what: A first pole and two lures; any fishing trainer teaches the rest.
Fishing.why: A fisher never goes hungry: any lake, river or sea becomes a source of food, and the catch can be cooked, sold or traded. Patient anglers even pull up treasure chests and rare fish worth a small fortune.

Herbalism.what: A herb pouch, and a few Peacebloom and Silverleaf to show what to look for.
Herbalism.why: Herbalists know which flowers and roots grow where and gather them on their travels. Alchemists and scribes pay well for them, and old herbal lore teaches how to draw a little healing from the plants themselves.

Inscription.what: The inking set, parchment, and Ivory Ink for the first scrolls.
Inscription.why: Scribes grind herbs into pigments and inks and write scrolls, glyphs that shape a fighter's abilities, and even decks of fortune cards. Every kind of fighter and spellcaster wants glyphs, so a scribe's work is always in demand.

Jewelcrafting.what: The Jeweler's Kit (the very first recipes do without it, but Malachite Pendant, Inlaid Malachite Ring, Bronze Setting and most later ones need it), copper bars for Delicate Copper Wire and the first rings, rough stone for a statue, and two Malachite.
Jewelcrafting.why: Jewelcrafters cut raw gems and set them into rings, necklaces and trinkets, and shape stones that add power to gear. They also prospect ore for hidden gems, so a little mining goes a long way.

Leatherworking.what: Leather and thread for the first pieces.
Leatherworking.why: Leatherworkers turn hides into sturdy armour for hunters, rogues, druids and shamans, along with armour kits that toughen any piece of gear. It pairs naturally with skinning, so the hunter supplies the craftsman.

Mining.what: The pick every miner needs (tool category Mining Pick).
Mining.why: Miners dig copper, tin, iron and rarer ores from the hills, the raw stuff every smith, engineer and jeweller needs. Ore always sells, and mining also toughens the body.

Skinning.what: The knife every skinner needs (tool category Skinning Knife).
Skinning.why: A skinner takes leather and hides from the beasts they hunt, so every wolf or boar brought down is worth something. Leather is always in demand among leatherworkers, and the work is said to sharpen a fighter's eye for a weak spot.

Tailoring.what: Linen (two make a bolt) and thread for the first pieces.
Tailoring.why: Tailors weave cloth taken from fallen foes into robes, shirts and, most valued of all, bags to carry more on the road. A good tailor never lacks for customers, since every traveller needs more room in their packs.
